title: Ordinary Abundance
excerpt: A walk through a modern apartment, through the eyes of the people for whom everything in it was new.
content_html:
Edward Bellamy once imagined that music on demand would be "the limit of human felicity." A modern apartment is full of things that once drew the same kind of awe.

The sitting room

The sitting room

It’s eight o’clock. The apartment is quiet, aside from the music playing softly over the speaker. It’s a playlist your friend made for you years ago. You send them a text to check in, then pick up a book, flick on the lamp, and settle into the chair to read.

Any song, at home

If we could have devised an arrangement for providing everybody with music in their homes, perfect in quality, unlimited in quantity, suited to every mood, and beginning and ceasing at will, we should have considered the limit of human felicity already attained.

Edward Bellamy, 1888 — From Looking Backward, his utopian novel set in the year 2000. Before recordings, listening to music meant having instruments or performers nearby, and favorite songs could go unheard for years at a time.

Light without fire

The people, almost with bated breath, stood overwhelmed with awe, as if in the presence of the supernatural. The strange, weird light, exceeded in power only by the sun, yet mild as moonlight, rendered the Court House square as light as midday.

A witness at Wabash, Indiana, 1880 — The night Wabash, Indiana became one of the first cities lit entirely by electric light. Candles, oil lamps, and gas jets gave relatively feeble light, and were all smoky open fires inside the home.

A museum on the wall

A museum without walls has been opened to us, and it will carry infinitely farther that limited revelation of the world of art which the real museums offer us within their walls.

André Malraux, 1947 — Le Musée imaginaire, later translated as Museum Without Walls. Before reliable reproduction, most people saw major artworks only by visiting churches, collections, or museums.

Memories kept

The very shadow of the person lying there fixed for ever! ... I would rather have such a memorial of one I dearly loved, than the noblest artist's work ever produced.

Elizabeth Barrett Browning, 1843 — On first seeing a daguerreotype, in a letter to Mary Russell Mitford. Preserving a likeness used to require a painted portrait; many families had no accurate image of relatives who died.

Reading after the eyes fail

It is not twenty years since there was discovered the art of making spectacles ... one of the best and most necessary in the world. I myself saw the man who discovered it, and I talked with him.

Friar Giordano da Pisa, 1306 — A sermon at Santa Maria Novella, Florence. Age-related vision loss was common, and before spectacles it could end reading and other close work.

Distant messaging

Of all the marvellous achievements of modern science, the Electric Telegraph is transcendently the greatest and most serviceable to mankind. It is a perpetual miracle, which no familiarity can render commonplace.

Briggs & Maverick, 1858 — The Story of the Telegraph. For most of history, messages traveled only as fast as the person who carried them. Receiving a reply from far away could take weeks or months.

Books unchained

A great good, and almost a divine benefit to the world.

Jakob Wimpfeling, 1505 — The German humanist, on the new art of printing. A hand-copied book was valuable enough that libraries chained theirs to the reading desks.

The kitchen

It’s nine. A chapter ends, and you stretch and wander into the kitchen. You’re not exactly sure what you want, so you aimlessly rifle through your fruit bowl, open and close the door to the fridge, and settle on a cup of tea. You lean against the counter and let your mind wander as the water comes to a boil.

Clean water on tap

Water! Water! is the universal note which is sounded through every part of the city, and infuses joy and exultation into the masses.

Philip Hone, 1842 — On the arrival of Croton water in New York City, in his diary. Manhattan’s wells shared soil with its privies and burial grounds; the cholera epidemic ten years earlier had killed 3,515 New Yorkers.

Fruit from afar

Like lovers' kisses, she biteth — she is a pleasure bordering on pain from the fierceness and insanity of her relish.

Charles Lamb, 1822 — On the rapture of the pineapple. In eighteenth-century Britain, a pineapple was costly enough that hostesses sometimes rented one for the evening rather than eat it.

Cold kept indoors

The first transport of ice from the shores of the United States to the banks of the Ganges is an event of no mean importance ... the names of those who planned and have successfully carried through their adventure at their own cost, deserve to be handed down to posterity with the name of other benefactors of mankind.

The Calcutta Courier, 1837 — On the arrival of New England pond-ice in tropical India. Without cold storage, perishable food like dairy and meat spoiled within a day, and most foods could not be kept or eaten out of season.

Eden in jars

It is said that these things come from the earthly paradise; for the wind blows down the trees in paradise, just as the wind blows down the dry wood in the forests of our own land.

Jean de Joinville, c. 1309 — On merchants who netted ginger, cinnamon and rhubarb from the Nile. In medieval price lists, a pound of ginger sold for the price of a sheep; a pound of saffron, the price of a horse.

The back room

At ten, the night starts to wind down. You wash your face, then wash down a pill with a glass of water. As you brush your teeth, you make a mental note of the last few chores you need to cross off the list tomorrow morning before heading to the airport.

Smallpox made historical

You have erased from the calendar of human afflictions one of its greatest. ... Future nations will know by history only that the loathsome smallpox has existed, and by you has been extirpated.

Thomas Jefferson, 1806 — In a letter celebrating Edward Jenner’s vaccine, sent to Jenner’s nephew. Smallpox killed about three of every ten people it infected, and in Jenner’s century it killed an estimated four hundred thousand Europeans a year.

Pain, interrupted

Before whom, in all time, surgery was agony; by whom pain in surgery was averted and annulled; since whom, science has controlled pain.

Epitaph of W. T. G. Morton, 1871 — Morton first publicly demonstrated ether anaesthesia. Before anesthesia, operations were performed with the patient conscious, and the primary means of managing pain were speed, alcohol, and opium.

The end of the outhouse

It just felt like I was the wealthiest person in the world. It felt great not to have to go outside to go to the restroom.

Patty Doak, 2003 — Recalling her family's first indoor bathroom, rural Iowa. Well into the twentieth century, most rural American homes had no indoor bathroom, and every gallon of water for cooking, washing, and bathing was carried in by hand.

Freedom on two wheels

I think it has done more to emancipate women than anything else in the world. I stand and rejoice every time I see a woman ride by on a wheel.

Susan B. Anthony, 1896 — Interviewed by Nellie Bly for the New York World. The safety bicycle opened up new possibilities for independent travel, especially for women under restrictive social rules.

The washtub retired

Come, Muse, and sing the dreaded Washing-Day. Ye who beneath the yoke of wedlock bend, With bowed soul, full well ye ken the day

Anna Laetitia Barbauld, 1797 — From her poem 'Washing-Day.' A household wash meant hauling and heating water by the barrel, then scrubbing, rinsing, and wringing every piece by hand; it filled an entire day each week.

The queen of inventions

What philanthropy failed to accomplish, what religion, poetry, eloquence, and reason had sought in vain, has been produced by — the Sewing Machine.

Godey's Lady's Book, 1860 — From 'The Queen of Inventions,' in the era's leading women's magazine. Before the machine, most people owned only two or three outfits, and a single new shirt meant some fourteen hours of hand stitching.

Warmth in every room

It is so cold that the freezing of the ink on the point of my pen renders it difficult to write. We have had the thermometer at 12°.

Thomas Jefferson, 1796 — In a letter to his son-in-law, the ink freezing as he wrote. Bedrooms in winter often fell close to the temperature outside, and it was not unusual to wake up to a frozen washbasin.

The old wish to fly

I sometimes think that the desire to fly after the fashion of birds is an ideal handed down to us by our ancestors who, in their grueling travels across trackless lands in prehistoric times, looked enviously on the birds soaring freely through space, at full speed, above all obstacles, on the infinite highway of the air.

Wilbur Wright, 1908 — Remarks at a banquet of the Aéro-Club de France, Paris. Before flight, crossing an ocean took a week or more at sea, and emigrating across one often meant never seeing your family again.

At eleven, you switch off the lights, silence your phone, and lie down to sleep. As your head hits the pillow, you idly wonder what people slept on before mattresses.

All the items in this room were once out of reach; some not yet invented, others too rare or costly for the vast majority of people. Today, most of us lucky enough to live with them walk past without a second thought.

It is to humanity’s credit that we remain restless in the midst of all of this progress. We continue to look forward, pushing the frontier further with new treatments, new tools, and new institutions that will help future generations in ways we can’t even picture yet.

But our lives today are a gallery of past generations’ heroic efforts to do the same. It serves us, and honors them, to recapture whenever possible the old sense of awe at these wonders that have long since become commonplace.

sentences.en: Before reliable reproduction, most people saw major artworks only by visiting churches, collections, or museums.
sentences.zh: 在可靠的复制品出现之前，大多数人只能通过参观教堂、收藏品或博物馆来欣赏主要艺术品。

blocks.html_en: Memories kept

sentences.en: Memories kept
sentences.zh: 保留的回忆

blocks.html_en: The very shadow of the person lying there fixed for ever! ... I would rather have such a memorial of one I dearly loved, than the noblest artist's work ever produced.

sentences.en: The very shadow of the person lying there fixed for ever! ...
sentences.zh: 躺在那里的人影永远定格了！ ...

sentences.en: I would rather have such a memorial of one I dearly loved, than the noblest artist's work ever produced.
sentences.zh: 我宁愿拥有这样一座我深爱的人的纪念碑，也不愿拥有有史以来最崇高的艺术家的作品。

blocks.html_en: Elizabeth Barrett Browning, 1843 — On first seeing a daguerreotype, in a letter to Mary Russell Mitford. Preserving a likeness used to require a painted portrait; many families had no accurate image of relatives who died.

sentences.en: Elizabeth Barrett Browning, 1843 — On first seeing a daguerreotype, in a letter to Mary Russell Mitford.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白·巴雷特·布朗宁 (Elizabeth Barrett Browning)，1843 年——第一次看到银版照片，是在给玛丽·拉塞尔·米特福德 (Mary Russell Mitford) 的一封信中。

sentences.en: Preserving a likeness used to require a painted portrait; many families had no accurate image of relatives who died.
sentences.zh: 保留过去需要绘制肖像的相似性；许多家庭对去世的亲人没有准确的印象。

blocks.html_en: Reading after the eyes fail

sentences.en: Reading after the eyes fail
sentences.zh: 眼睛失明后读书

blocks.html_en: It is not twenty years since there was discovered the art of making spectacles ... one of the best and most necessary in the world. I myself saw the man who discovered it, and I talked with him.

sentences.en: It is not twenty years since there was discovered the art of making spectacles ...
sentences.zh: 距离制造眼镜的艺术被发现还不到二十年......

sentences.en: one of the best and most necessary in the world.
sentences.zh: 世界上最好和最必要的之一。

sentences.en: I myself saw the man who discovered it, and I talked with him.
sentences.zh: 我亲自见到了发现它的人，并与他交谈。

blocks.html_en: Friar Giordano da Pisa, 1306 — A sermon at Santa Maria Novella, Florence. Age-related vision loss was common, and before spectacles it could end reading and other close work.

sentences.en: Friar Giordano da Pisa, 1306 — A sermon at Santa Maria Novella, Florence.
sentences.zh: 佐丹奴·达比萨修士，1306 年 — 在佛罗伦萨新圣母玛利亚教堂的布道。

sentences.en: Age-related vision loss was common, and before spectacles it could end reading and other close work.
sentences.zh: 与年龄相关的视力丧失很常见，在戴眼镜之前，它可能会导致阅读和其他近距离工作的结束。

blocks.html_en: Distant messaging

sentences.en: Distant messaging
sentences.zh: 远程消息传递

blocks.html_en: Of all the marvellous achievements of modern science, the Electric Telegraph is transcendently the greatest and most serviceable to mankind. It is a perpetual miracle, which no familiarity can render commonplace.

sentences.en: Of all the marvellous achievements of modern science, the Electric Telegraph is transcendently the greatest and most serviceable to mankind.
sentences.zh: 在现代科学的所有非凡成就中，电报无疑是最伟大、对人类最有用的。

sentences.en: It is a perpetual miracle, which no familiarity can render commonplace.
sentences.zh: 这是一个永恒的奇迹，任何熟悉都无法使其变得司空见惯。

blocks.html_en: Briggs & Maverick, 1858 — The Story of the Telegraph. For most of history, messages traveled only as fast as the person who carried them. Receiving a reply from far away could take weeks or months.

sentences.en: Briggs & Maverick, 1858 — The Story of the Telegraph.
sentences.zh: Briggs & Maverick，1858 年 — 电报的故事。

sentences.en: For most of history, messages traveled only as fast as the person who carried them.
sentences.zh: 在历史的大部分时间里，信息传播的速度取决于携带信息的人。

sentences.en: Receiving a reply from far away could take weeks or months.
sentences.zh: 收到来自远方的回复可能需要数周或数月的时间。

blocks.html_en: Books unchained

sentences.en: Books unchained
sentences.zh: 书本不受束缚

blocks.html_en: A great good, and almost a divine benefit to the world.

sentences.en: A great good, and almost a divine benefit to the world.
sentences.zh: 这是对世界的伟大善事，几乎是神圣的利益。

blocks.html_en: Jakob Wimpfeling, 1505 — The German humanist, on the new art of printing. A hand-copied book was valuable enough that libraries chained theirs to the reading desks.

sentences.en: Jakob Wimpfeling, 1505 — The German humanist, on the new art of printing.
sentences.zh: 雅各布·温普费林 (Jakob Wimpfeling)，1505 年 — 德国人文主义者，论新印刷艺术。

sentences.en: A hand-copied book was valuable enough that libraries chained theirs to the reading desks.
sentences.zh: 一本手抄的书很有价值，以至于图书馆把它们挂在阅览桌上。

blocks.html_en: The kitchen

sentences.en: The kitchen
sentences.zh: 厨房

blocks.html_en: It’s nine. A chapter ends, and you stretch and wander into the kitchen. You’re not exactly sure what you want, so you aimlessly rifle through your fruit bowl, open and close the door to the fridge, and settle on a cup of tea. You lean against the counter and let your mind wander as the water comes to a boil.

sentences.en: It’s nine.
sentences.zh: 九点了。

sentences.en: A chapter ends, and you stretch and wander into the kitchen.
sentences.zh: 一章结束了，你伸了个懒腰，漫步走进厨房。

sentences.en: You’re not exactly sure what you want, so you aimlessly rifle through your fruit bowl, open and close the door to the fridge, and settle on a cup of tea.
sentences.zh: 你不确定自己想要什么，所以你漫无目的地翻阅水果盘，打开和关闭冰箱门，然后选择了一杯茶。

sentences.en: You lean against the counter and let your mind wander as the water comes to a boil.
sentences.zh: 当水沸腾时，你靠在柜台上，任由思绪飘游。

blocks.html_en: Clean water on tap

sentences.en: Clean water on tap
sentences.zh: 自来水干净

blocks.html_en: Water! Water! is the universal note which is sounded through every part of the city, and infuses joy and exultation into the masses.

sentences.en: Water!
sentences.zh: 水！

sentences.en: Water!
sentences.zh: 水！

sentences.en: is the universal note which is sounded through every part of the city, and infuses joy and exultation into the masses.
sentences.zh: 这是响彻城市各个角落的普遍音符，为群众注入了欢乐和欢腾。

blocks.html_en: Philip Hone, 1842 — On the arrival of Croton water in New York City, in his diary. Manhattan’s wells shared soil with its privies and burial grounds; the cholera epidemic ten years earlier had killed 3,515 New Yorkers.

sentences.en: Philip Hone, 1842 — On the arrival of Croton water in New York City, in his diary.
sentences.zh: 菲利普·霍恩 (Philip Hone)，1842 年——在他的日记中，讲述了巴豆水到达纽约市的情况。

sentences.en: Manhattan’s wells shared soil with its privies and burial grounds; the cholera epidemic ten years earlier had killed 3,515 New Yorkers.
sentences.zh: 曼哈顿的水井与厕所和墓地共享土壤。十年前的霍乱疫情已导致 3,515 名纽约人死亡。

blocks.html_en: Fruit from afar

sentences.en: Fruit from afar
sentences.zh: 远方来的果子

blocks.html_en: Like lovers' kisses, she biteth — she is a pleasure bordering on pain from the fierceness and insanity of her relish.

sentences.en: Like lovers' kisses, she biteth — she is a pleasure bordering on pain from the fierceness and insanity of her relish.
sentences.zh: 就像恋人的吻一样，她咬人——她的享受带来了一种近乎痛苦的快感，因为她的享受的激烈和疯狂。

blocks.html_en: Charles Lamb, 1822 — On the rapture of the pineapple. In eighteenth-century Britain, a pineapple was costly enough that hostesses sometimes rented one for the evening rather than eat it.

sentences.en: Charles Lamb, 1822 — On the rapture of the pineapple.
sentences.zh: 查尔斯·兰姆 (Charles Lamb)，1822 年 — 论菠萝的狂喜。

sentences.en: In eighteenth-century Britain, a pineapple was costly enough that hostesses sometimes rented one for the evening rather than eat it.
sentences.zh: 在十八世纪的英国，一个菠萝非常昂贵，以至于女主人有时会租一个晚上而不是吃它。

blocks.html_en: Cold kept indoors

sentences.en: Cold kept indoors
sentences.zh: 冷藏在室内

blocks.html_en: The first transport of ice from the shores of the United States to the banks of the Ganges is an event of no mean importance ... the names of those who planned and have successfully carried through their adventure at their own cost, deserve to be handed down to posterity with the name of other benefactors of mankind.

sentences.en: The first transport of ice from the shores of the United States to the banks of the Ganges is an event of no mean importance ...
sentences.zh: 首次将冰块从美国海岸运至恒河岸是一件意义非凡的事件……

sentences.en: the names of those who planned and have successfully carried through their adventure at their own cost, deserve to be handed down to posterity with the name of other benefactors of mankind.
sentences.zh: 那些计划并以自己的代价成功完成冒险的人的名字应该与人类其他捐助者的名字一起流传后世。

blocks.html_en: The Calcutta Courier, 1837 — On the arrival of New England pond-ice in tropical India. Without cold storage, perishable food like dairy and meat spoiled within a day, and most foods could not be kept or eaten out of season.

sentences.en: The Calcutta Courier, 1837 — On the arrival of New England pond-ice in tropical India.
sentences.zh: 《加尔各答信使报》，1837 年——新英格兰池塘冰到达热带印度。

sentences.en: Without cold storage, perishable food like dairy and meat spoiled within a day, and most foods could not be kept or eaten out of season.
sentences.zh: 如果没有冷藏，乳制品和肉类等易腐烂食品一天之内就会变质，而且大多数食品都无法保存或反季节食用。

blocks.html_en: Eden in jars

sentences.en: Eden in jars
sentences.zh: 罐子里的伊甸园

blocks.html_en: It is said that these things come from the earthly paradise; for the wind blows down the trees in paradise, just as the wind blows down the dry wood in the forests of our own land.

sentences.en: It is said that these things come from the earthly paradise; for the wind blows down the trees in paradise, just as the wind blows down the dry wood in the forests of our own land.
sentences.zh: 据说这些东西来自人间天堂；因为风吹倒了天堂里的树木，就像风吹倒了我们自己土地上森林里的干木头一样。

blocks.html_en: Jean de Joinville, c. 1309 — On merchants who netted ginger, cinnamon and rhubarb from the Nile. In medieval price lists, a pound of ginger sold for the price of a sheep; a pound of saffron, the price of a horse.

sentences.en: Jean de Joinville, c.
sentences.zh: 让·德·茹安维尔，c.

sentences.en: 1309 — On merchants who netted ginger, cinnamon and rhubarb from the Nile.
sentences.zh: 1309 年——商人从尼罗河捕获生姜、肉桂和大黄。

sentences.en: In medieval price lists, a pound of ginger sold for the price of a sheep; a pound of saffron, the price of a horse.
sentences.zh: 在中世纪的价目表中，一磅生姜的售价是一只羊的价格；一磅藏红花相当于一匹马的价格。

blocks.html_en: The back room

sentences.en: The back room
sentences.zh: 后面的房间

blocks.html_en: At ten, the night starts to wind down. You wash your face, then wash down a pill with a glass of water. As you brush your teeth, you make a mental note of the last few chores you need to cross off the list tomorrow morning before heading to the airport.

sentences.en: At ten, the night starts to wind down.
sentences.zh: 十点钟，夜幕开始降临。

sentences.en: You wash your face, then wash down a pill with a glass of water.
sentences.zh: 你洗脸，然后用一杯水冲下一颗药丸。

sentences.en: As you brush your teeth, you make a mental note of the last few chores you need to cross off the list tomorrow morning before heading to the airport.
sentences.zh: 当你刷牙时，你会在心里记下明天早上前往机场之前需要划掉清单上的最后几项家务。

blocks.html_en: Smallpox made historical

sentences.en: Smallpox made historical
sentences.zh: 天花创造了历史

blocks.html_en: You have erased from the calendar of human afflictions one of its greatest. ... Future nations will know by history only that the loathsome smallpox has existed, and by you has been extirpated.

sentences.en: You have erased from the calendar of human afflictions one of its greatest. ...
sentences.zh: 你们已经从人类苦难的日历中抹去了其中最大的苦难之一。 ...

sentences.en: Future nations will know by history only that the loathsome smallpox has existed, and by you has been extirpated.
sentences.zh: 未来的国家只会从历史中知道，令人厌恶的天花曾经存在过，并且被你们消灭了。

blocks.html_en: Thomas Jefferson, 1806 — In a letter celebrating Edward Jenner’s vaccine, sent to Jenner’s nephew. Smallpox killed about three of every ten people it infected, and in Jenner’s century it killed an estimated four hundred thousand Europeans a year.

sentences.en: Thomas Jefferson, 1806 — In a letter celebrating Edward Jenner’s vaccine, sent to Jenner’s nephew.
sentences.zh: 托马斯·杰斐逊，1806 年——一封写给詹纳侄子的庆祝爱德华·詹纳接种疫苗的信。

sentences.en: Smallpox killed about three of every ten people it infected, and in Jenner’s century it killed an estimated four hundred thousand Europeans a year.
sentences.zh: 天花大约每十名感染者中就有三人死亡，在詹纳的世纪，每年估计有四十万欧洲人死于天花。

blocks.html_en: Pain, interrupted

sentences.en: Pain, interrupted
sentences.zh: 疼痛，中断

blocks.html_en: Before whom, in all time, surgery was agony; by whom pain in surgery was averted and annulled; since whom, science has controlled pain.

sentences.en: Before whom, in all time, surgery was agony; by whom pain in surgery was averted and annulled; since whom, science has controlled pain.
sentences.zh: 在他们面前，手术一直都是痛苦的；他避免并消除了手术中的疼痛；从他开始，科学就控制了疼痛。

blocks.html_en: Epitaph of W. T. G. Morton, 1871 — Morton first publicly demonstrated ether anaesthesia. Before anesthesia, operations were performed with the patient conscious, and the primary means of managing pain were speed, alcohol, and opium.

sentences.en: Epitaph of W.
sentences.zh: W.的墓志铭

sentences.en: T.
sentences.zh: T。

sentences.en: G.
sentences.zh: G。

sentences.en: Morton, 1871 — Morton first publicly demonstrated ether anaesthesia.
sentences.zh: 莫顿，1871 年——莫顿首次公开演示乙醚麻醉。

sentences.en: Before anesthesia, operations were performed with the patient conscious, and the primary means of managing pain were speed, alcohol, and opium.
sentences.zh: 麻醉前，手术是在病人神志清醒的情况下进行的，控制疼痛的主要手段是速度、酒精和鸦片。

blocks.html_en: The end of the outhouse

sentences.en: The end of the outhouse
sentences.zh: 外屋的尽头

blocks.html_en: It just felt like I was the wealthiest person in the world. It felt great not to have to go outside to go to the restroom.

sentences.en: It just felt like I was the wealthiest person in the world.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像我是世界上最富有的人。

sentences.en: It felt great not to have to go outside to go to the restroom.
sentences.zh: 不用去外面上厕所的感觉真好。

blocks.html_en: Patty Doak, 2003 — Recalling her family's first indoor bathroom, rural Iowa. Well into the twentieth century, most rural American homes had no indoor bathroom, and every gallon of water for cooking, washing, and bathing was carried in by hand.

sentences.en: Patty Doak, 2003 — Recalling her family's first indoor bathroom, rural Iowa.
sentences.zh: 帕蒂·多克 (Patty Doak)，2003 年 — 回忆起她家在爱荷华州乡村的第一个室内浴室。

sentences.en: Well into the twentieth century, most rural American homes had no indoor bathroom, and every gallon of water for cooking, washing, and bathing was carried in by hand.
sentences.zh: 进入二十世纪，大多数美国农村家庭都没有室内浴室，做饭、洗衣和洗澡的每一加仑水都是用手运进来的。

blocks.html_en: Freedom on two wheels

sentences.en: Freedom on two wheels
sentences.zh: 两轮自由

blocks.html_en: I think it has done more to emancipate women than anything else in the world. I stand and rejoice every time I see a woman ride by on a wheel.

sentences.en: I think it has done more to emancipate women than anything else in the world.
sentences.zh: 我认为它在解放妇女方面所做的贡献比世界上任何其他事情都多。

sentences.en: I stand and rejoice every time I see a woman ride by on a wheel.
sentences.zh: 每当我看到一个女人骑着轮子经过时，我都会站起来很高兴。

blocks.html_en: Susan B. Anthony, 1896 — Interviewed by Nellie Bly for the New York World. The safety bicycle opened up new possibilities for independent travel, especially for women under restrictive social rules.

sentences.en: Susan B.
sentences.zh: 苏珊·B.

sentences.en: Anthony, 1896 — Interviewed by Nellie Bly for the New York World.
sentences.zh: 安东尼，1896 年 — 接受《纽约世界》内莉·布莱 (Nellie Bly) 的采访。

sentences.en: The safety bicycle opened up new possibilities for independent travel, especially for women under restrictive social rules.
sentences.zh: 安全自行车为独立旅行开辟了新的可能性，特别是对于受到社会规则限制的女性而言。

blocks.html_en: The washtub retired

sentences.en: The washtub retired
sentences.zh: 洗衣盆退役了

blocks.html_en: Come, Muse, and sing the dreaded Washing-Day. Ye who beneath the yoke of wedlock bend, With bowed soul, full well ye ken the day

sentences.en: Come, Muse, and sing the dreaded Washing-Day.
sentences.zh: 来吧，缪斯，唱响可怕的洗涤日。

sentences.en: Ye who beneath the yoke of wedlock bend, With bowed soul, full well ye ken the day
sentences.zh: 你们那些在婚姻的枷锁下屈服的人，带着低头的灵魂，你们今天过得很好

blocks.html_en: Anna Laetitia Barbauld, 1797 — From her poem 'Washing-Day.' A household wash meant hauling and heating water by the barrel, then scrubbing, rinsing, and wringing every piece by hand; it filled an entire day each week.

sentences.en: Anna Laetitia Barbauld, 1797 — From her poem 'Washing-Day.'
sentences.zh: 安娜·莱蒂希娅·巴鲍德 (Anna Laetitia Barbaud)，1797 年 — 摘自她的诗《洗涤日》。

sentences.en: A household wash meant hauling and heating water by the barrel, then scrubbing, rinsing, and wringing every piece by hand; it filled an entire day each week.
sentences.zh: 家庭洗涤意味着用桶拉水并加热，然后用手擦洗、漂洗并拧干每一块；每周都占据一整天的时间。

blocks.html_en: The queen of inventions

sentences.en: The queen of inventions
sentences.zh: 发明女王

blocks.html_en: What philanthropy failed to accomplish, what religion, poetry, eloquence, and reason had sought in vain, has been produced by — the Sewing Machine.

sentences.en: What philanthropy failed to accomplish, what religion, poetry, eloquence, and reason had sought in vain, has been produced by — the Sewing Machine.
sentences.zh: 慈善事业未能实现的东西，宗教、诗歌、雄辩和理性徒劳地寻求的东西，已经由缝纫机生产出来了。

blocks.html_en: Godey's Lady's Book, 1860 — From 'The Queen of Inventions,' in the era's leading women's magazine. Before the machine, most people owned only two or three outfits, and a single new shirt meant some fourteen hours of hand stitching.

sentences.en: Godey's Lady's Book, 1860 — From 'The Queen of Inventions,' in the era's leading women's magazine.
sentences.zh: 戈迪的《女士之书》，1860 年 — 摘自当时领先的女性杂志《发明女王》。

sentences.en: Before the machine, most people owned only two or three outfits, and a single new shirt meant some fourteen hours of hand stitching.
sentences.zh: 在机器出现之前，大多数人只拥有两三套衣服，一件新衬衫意味着大约十四个小时的手工缝制。

blocks.html_en: Warmth in every room

sentences.en: Warmth in every room
sentences.zh: 每个房间都充满温暖

blocks.html_en: It is so cold that the freezing of the ink on the point of my pen renders it difficult to write. We have had the thermometer at 12°.

sentences.en: It is so cold that the freezing of the ink on the point of my pen renders it difficult to write.
sentences.zh: 天太冷了，笔尖上的墨水都结冰了，写起来很困难。

sentences.en: We have had the thermometer at 12°.
sentences.zh: 我们的温度计是12°。

blocks.html_en: Thomas Jefferson, 1796 — In a letter to his son-in-law, the ink freezing as he wrote. Bedrooms in winter often fell close to the temperature outside, and it was not unusual to wake up to a frozen washbasin.

sentences.en: Thomas Jefferson, 1796 — In a letter to his son-in-law, the ink freezing as he wrote.
sentences.zh: 托马斯·杰斐逊 (Thomas Jefferson)，1796 年——在写给女婿的一封信中，他写下的墨水凝固了。

sentences.en: Bedrooms in winter often fell close to the temperature outside, and it was not unusual to wake up to a frozen washbasin.
sentences.zh: 冬天的卧室温度常常接近室外，醒来发现脸盆结冰的情况并不罕见。

blocks.html_en: The old wish to fly

sentences.en: The old wish to fly
sentences.zh: 旧时的愿望飞翔

blocks.html_en: I sometimes think that the desire to fly after the fashion of birds is an ideal handed down to us by our ancestors who, in their grueling travels across trackless lands in prehistoric times, looked enviously on the birds soaring freely through space, at full speed, above all obstacles, on the infinite highway of the air.

sentences.en: I sometimes think that the desire to fly after the fashion of birds is an ideal handed down to us by our ancestors who, in their grueling travels across trackless lands in prehistoric times, looked enviously on the birds soaring freely through space, at full speed, above all obstacles, on the infinite highway of the air.
sentences.zh: 有时我会想，追随鸟类飞翔的愿望是我们的祖先传给我们的理想，他们在史前时代艰苦跋涉，穿越无路可走的土地时，羡慕地看着鸟儿在太空中全速自由翱翔，越过一切障碍，在无限的空中高速公路上。

content_html_zh:
爱德华·贝拉米曾经想象音乐点播将是“人类幸福的极限”。 现代化的公寓里充满了曾经令人敬畏的东西。

滚动浏览公寓

客厅

客厅

现在是八点钟。 公寓里很安静，除了扬声器里轻柔地播放着音乐。 这是您的朋友多年前为您制作的播放列表。 你给他们发一条短信来登记，然后拿起一本书，打开灯，坐在椅子上看书。

在家听什么歌都可以

如果我们能够设计出一种安排，为每个人在家中提供质量完美、数量无限、适合各种心情、随意开始和结束的音乐，我们就应该考虑到人类幸福已经达到的极限。

爱德华·贝拉米，1888 年——《回顾过去》，他的乌托邦小说，背景设定在 2000 年。 在录音之前，听音乐意味着附近有乐器或表演者，而最喜欢的歌曲可能会好几年都听不到。

光无火

人们几乎屏住了呼吸，敬畏地站在那里，仿佛看到了超自然的存在。 奇异的光芒，威力仅次于太阳，却又如月光般温和，将法院广场照得如同正午般明亮。

1880 年，印第安纳州沃巴什的一位见证者——那天晚上，印第安纳州沃巴什成为首批完全被电灯照亮的城市之一。 蜡烛、油灯和煤气灯的光线相对较弱，屋内都是冒着烟的明火。

墙上的博物馆

一座没有围墙的博物馆向我们敞开了大门，它将把真正的博物馆在围墙内为我们提供的有限的艺术世界的揭示无限地带向更远的地方。

安德烈·马尔罗 (André Malraux)，1947 年——《想象中的博物馆》，后译为《无墙博物馆》。 在可靠的复制品出现之前，大多数人只能通过参观教堂、收藏品或博物馆来欣赏主要艺术品。

保留的回忆

躺在那里的人影永远定格了！ ... 我宁愿拥有这样一座我深爱的人的纪念碑，也不愿拥有有史以来最崇高的艺术家的作品。

伊丽莎白·巴雷特·布朗宁 (Elizabeth Barrett Browning)，1843 年——第一次看到银版照片，是在给玛丽·拉塞尔·米特福德 (Mary Russell Mitford) 的一封信中。 保留过去需要绘制肖像的相似性；许多家庭对去世的亲人没有准确的印象。

眼睛失明后读书

距离制造眼镜的艺术被发现还不到二十年...... 世界上最好和最必要的之一。 我亲自见到了发现它的人，并与他交谈。

佐丹奴·达比萨修士，1306 年 — 在佛罗伦萨新圣母玛利亚教堂的布道。 与年龄相关的视力丧失很常见，在戴眼镜之前，它可能会导致阅读和其他近距离工作的结束。

远程消息传递

在现代科学的所有非凡成就中，电报无疑是最伟大、对人类最有用的。 这是一个永恒的奇迹，任何熟悉都无法使其变得司空见惯。

Briggs & Maverick，1858 年 — 电报的故事。 在历史的大部分时间里，信息传播的速度取决于携带信息的人。 收到来自远方的回复可能需要数周或数月的时间。

书本不受束缚

这是对世界的伟大善事，几乎是神圣的利益。

雅各布·温普费林 (Jakob Wimpfeling)，1505 年 — 德国人文主义者，论新印刷艺术。 一本手抄的书很有价值，以至于图书馆把它们挂在阅览桌上。

厨房

九点了。 一章结束了，你伸了个懒腰，漫步走进厨房。 你不确定自己想要什么，所以你漫无目的地翻阅水果盘，打开和关闭冰箱门，然后选择了一杯茶。 当水沸腾时，你靠在柜台上，任由思绪飘游。

自来水干净

水！ 水！ 这是响彻城市各个角落的普遍音符，为群众注入了欢乐和欢腾。

菲利普·霍恩 (Philip Hone)，1842 年——在他的日记中，讲述了巴豆水到达纽约市的情况。 曼哈顿的水井与厕所和墓地共享土壤。十年前的霍乱疫情已导致 3,515 名纽约人死亡。

远方来的果子

就像恋人的吻一样，她咬人——她的享受带来了一种近乎痛苦的快感，因为她的享受的激烈和疯狂。

查尔斯·兰姆 (Charles Lamb)，1822 年 — 论菠萝的狂喜。 在十八世纪的英国，一个菠萝非常昂贵，以至于女主人有时会租一个晚上而不是吃它。

冷藏在室内

首次将冰块从美国海岸运至恒河岸是一件意义非凡的事件…… 那些计划并以自己的代价成功完成冒险的人的名字应该与人类其他捐助者的名字一起流传后世。

《加尔各答信使报》，1837 年——新英格兰池塘冰到达热带印度。 如果没有冷藏，乳制品和肉类等易腐烂食品一天之内就会变质，而且大多数食品都无法保存或反季节食用。

罐子里的伊甸园

据说这些东西来自人间天堂；因为风吹倒了天堂里的树木，就像风吹倒了我们自己土地上森林里的干木头一样。

让·德·茹安维尔，c. 1309 年——商人从尼罗河捕获生姜、肉桂和大黄。 在中世纪的价目表中，一磅生姜的售价是一只羊的价格；一磅藏红花相当于一匹马的价格。

后面的房间

十点钟，夜幕开始降临。 你洗脸，然后用一杯水冲下一颗药丸。 当你刷牙时，你会在心里记下明天早上前往机场之前需要划掉清单上的最后几项家务。

天花创造了历史

你们已经从人类苦难的日历中抹去了其中最大的苦难之一。 ... 未来的国家只会从历史中知道，令人厌恶的天花曾经存在过，并且被你们消灭了。

托马斯·杰斐逊，1806 年——一封写给詹纳侄子的庆祝爱德华·詹纳接种疫苗的信。 天花大约每十名感染者中就有三人死亡，在詹纳的世纪，每年估计有四十万欧洲人死于天花。

疼痛，中断

在他们面前，手术一直都是痛苦的；他避免并消除了手术中的疼痛；从他开始，科学就控制了疼痛。

W.的墓志铭 T。 G。 莫顿，1871 年——莫顿首次公开演示乙醚麻醉。 麻醉前，手术是在病人神志清醒的情况下进行的，控制疼痛的主要手段是速度、酒精和鸦片。

外屋的尽头

感觉就像我是世界上最富有的人。 不用去外面上厕所的感觉真好。

帕蒂·多克 (Patty Doak)，2003 年 — 回忆起她家在爱荷华州乡村的第一个室内浴室。 进入二十世纪，大多数美国农村家庭都没有室内浴室，做饭、洗衣和洗澡的每一加仑水都是用手运进来的。

两轮自由

我认为它在解放妇女方面所做的贡献比世界上任何其他事情都多。 每当我看到一个女人骑着轮子经过时，我都会站起来很高兴。

苏珊·B. 安东尼，1896 年 — 接受《纽约世界》内莉·布莱 (Nellie Bly) 的采访。 安全自行车为独立旅行开辟了新的可能性，特别是对于受到社会规则限制的女性而言。

洗衣盆退役了

来吧，缪斯，唱响可怕的洗涤日。 你们那些在婚姻的枷锁下屈服的人，带着低头的灵魂，你们今天过得很好

安娜·莱蒂希娅·巴鲍德 (Anna Laetitia Barbaud)，1797 年 — 摘自她的诗《洗涤日》。 家庭洗涤意味着用桶拉水并加热，然后用手擦洗、漂洗并拧干每一块；每周都占据一整天的时间。

发明女王

慈善事业未能实现的东西，宗教、诗歌、雄辩和理性徒劳地寻求的东西，已经由缝纫机生产出来了。
